was: Idaho Panhandle NF (Coeur d'Alene River RD) campground set back in forest near the east shore of Hayden Lake (Mokins Bay); the lake is about a 10-minute walk from the loop. Single 14-site loop, RVs/trailers to 50 ft, paved spurs, drinking water, vault toilets, no hookups/dump/showers. Winding paved access road but suitable for larger rigs. Both first-come, first-served and reservable sites (reservable online). --Claude

was: Idaho Panhandle NF (Coeur d'Alene River area), on the North Fork Coeur d'Alene River off FH208 ~17 mi N of Prichard. ~30 drive-in sites with paved parking spurs, RVs to 45 ft; vault toilets, hand-pump drinking water, no hookups. Reservable online (unreserved sites go FCFS). --Claude
note: Idaho Panhandle NF (Coeur d'Alene River area), on the North Fork Coeur d'Alene River off FH208 ~17 mi N of Prichard. Drive-in sites with paved parking spurs; hand-pump drinking water. Reservable online (unreserved sites go FCFS). --Claude

was: USACE Albeni Falls Project (Riley Creek Recreation Area), the largest rec area, on the Pend Oreille River at Laclede. 67 sites all with electric+water hookups (50/30/20 amp), paved roads, dump station, hot showers, boat ramp, swim beach, playground; RVs to ~44 ft (no pull-throughs, drive-in tight for big rigs). Reservation only (no FCFS), reservable online. --Claude

was: USACE Albeni Falls Project, 'The Mudhole,' at the mouth of the Priest River on the Pend Oreille River, ~1 mi E of Priest River off Hwy 2. 20 drive-in sites, no hookups but on-site RV dump station; flush toilets, hot showers, boat ramp, swim beach, playground; loop paved in 2024. Reservation only (no FCFS), reservable online. --Claude

was: USFS (Idaho Panhandle NF, Priest Lake RD) campground on the west shore near the south end of Priest Lake. 15 drive-in sites (10 reservable, 5 FCFS) fitting RVs/trailers ~20-64 ft; vault toilets. Reservable online. --Claude
note: USFS (Idaho Panhandle NF, Priest Lake RD) campground on the west shore near the south end of Priest Lake. Drive-in sites (10 reservable, 5 FCFS) fitting RVs/trailers ~20-64 ft. Reservable online. --Claude

was: USFS (Idaho Panhandle NF, Priest Lake RD) campground on the west shore of Priest Lake. 24 sites (some FCFS, rest reservable), paved roads/spurs fitting RVs/trailers ~19-55 ft, flush toilets, pressurized water, sandy beach sloping to the lake. Reservable online. --Claude

was: BLM developed park on the east side of Salmon Falls Creek Reservoir, ~7 mi west of Rogerson near Salmon Dam. ~20 developed sites with shade cabanas, fire rings, tables and vault toilets; potable water, RV dump and boat ramp; dispersed sites also. First-come, first-served ($5 day-use). --Claude

was: Twin Falls County park in Salmon Falls Creek canyon south of Buhl, at the creek crossing below the Balanced Rock formation. ~12 informal primitive drive-in sites along the creek; pit toilets, potable water spigots, fire rings/grills and a rentable pavilion; no hookups. First-come, first-served, 7-day limit. --Claude

was: BLM campground (Pocatello Field Office) on the southwest shore of Blackfoot Reservoir near Soda Springs; RV Life mis-tagged as DNR. 28 campsites: 16 fully developed with 50-amp electric + potable water and 12 standard; 2 boat ramps, RV dump station. Mostly first-come, first-served (5 sites #10,11,13,14,16 reservable on recreation.gov). Drive-in RV accessible. --Claude

was: BLM Cove Recreation Site (Four Rivers Field Office) on CJ Strike Reservoir, ~8 mi NW of Bruneau; RV Life mis-tagged as DNR. 41 campsites (34 with cabana shade shelters over concrete pads) on packed-gravel/natural loops, no hookups, potable water, RV dump station, fishing docks, boat ramp. First-come, first-served, 14-day limit. Drive-in RV accessible. --Claude
note: BLM Cove Recreation Site (Four Rivers Field Office) on CJ Strike Reservoir, ~8 mi NW of Bruneau. 41 campsites (34 with cabana shade shelters over concrete pads) on packed-gravel/natural loops, fishing docks, boat ramp. Drive-in RV accessible. --Claude

was: BLM campground in the historic Silver City mining town, Owyhee Mtns ~23 mi of gravel road S of Murphy. 6 sites, first-come, first-served; no potable water (Jordan Creek is mercury-contaminated from old mining — bring water), vault toilets. The Murphy/Hwy-78 approach is well-packed gravel and a 24-ft C-class rig (towing a trailer) has driven in per a firsthand report; high-clearance advised, seasonal (Memorial Day to first snow). --Claude

was: BLM-managed semi-developed/dispersed camping around Magic Reservoir (sites incl. Lava Creek, Lava Cove, West Magic, Magic Dam, Myrtle Point); this area is shoreline pull-offs near the dam. Vault toilets, no drinking water, gravel/dirt drive-in access, no hookups. First-come, first-served (new $10/day boat-ramp fee at Magic/Moonstone/West Magic ramps). --Claude

was: BLM access site on the north shore of Magic Reservoir with a boat ramp/dock. One developed campsite (metal table, fire ring w/ grill, gravel drive) plus 3-4 primitive sites (stone rings, dirt drives); vault toilet, no water, no hookups. First-come, first-served (new $10/day boat-ramp fee). --Claude

was: BLM campground in a cottonwood gallery forest on the South Fork Snake River, ~23 mi NE of Idaho Falls (gravel access road off Kelly Canyon rd). 14 single sites ($10) + doubles, pull-throughs, central water spigot, vault toilets, day-use area, boat access; no hookups; pets not permitted; seasonal gate (May-Sep). Singles FCFS; 1 group site (fits ~4 large RVs) reservable online. --Claude

First-come, first-served (scan-and-pay via rec.gov app). --Claude

was: Caribou-Targhee NF (Ashton/Island Park RD) on the backwaters of Island Park Reservoir at the McCrea Bridge over Henrys Fork. 19 single + 4 double sites, no hookups, vault toilets, drinking water, boat ramp in the campground; RVs to 65 ft. Reservable online in season (FCFS after hours). Reservoir draws down for irrigation and by August water recedes from the campground. --Claude

was: Valley County Parks & Recreation (managed since 2026 in partnership with Idaho Fish & Game), ~9 mi E of Cascade on 260-acre Horsethief Reservoir (no-wake, 5 mph). Primitive; several loops (King's Landing, Bear Knob, Easters Cove, Timber Bay, Osprey) on the N/NW shore, vault toilets, potable water, fire pits, no hookups. Suitable for rigs 30 ft and under. Cash or check, first-come, first-served. --Claude

was: BLM Cottonwood Field Office campground on the Lower Salmon River, ~2.7 mi off Hwy 95 west of White Bird; popular boater put-in. 12 RV/tent sites, drinking water, flush & vault toilets, RV dump station, changing rooms, boat ramp; no hookups. First-come, first-served ($10/night). --Claude

was: BLM Cottonwood Field Office campground on the Clearwater River ~5 mi west of Orofino. 15 full-hookup RV sites (water/30-amp/sewer, RVs to 40 ft; 2 pull-through, rest back-in) plus 3 tent sites, flush & vault toilets, potable water, boat ramp, full-time camp host. was: Small Idaho State Park on 58-acre Round Lake near Sagle. Campground has 51 sites: 16 serviced back-in sites with 30-amp electric + water (max RV ~24 ft), plus standard sites; flush toilets, showers, dump station. BLM land leased to Jerome County and run by the local Snake River Canyons Park board. 13 level paved RV pads (pull-in/pull-through) with picnic table + fire ring, 2 vault toilets, no hookups; separate equestrian/overflow area (general campground, not horse-only). First-come, first-served, 5-night limit. --Claude
